name: website
description: The public landing page, sharing the app's tokens and branding.
parts: Keyboard skip link to the main content.
Brand, primary navigation, language dropdown and download link.
The language dropdown and download link.
Native popover button with the current language flag and name.
Language links with flags; aria-current marks the current page.
A link styled as a button; data-variant is primary or small when set.
Introduction and desktop and console screenshots.
The main heading, introduction and actions.
A decorative accent beside the introduction.
Download and source link groups, including platform installer choices.
A text link to a project resource.
Actual app captures with a sample library, linking to the full images.
The cropped desktop screenshot and its link to the full capture.
The cropped console screenshot and its link to the full capture.
A mode label below a screenshot.
The introductory video and its direct YouTube link.
A responsive, lazy-loaded YouTube privacy-enhanced embed.
The library, household and emulation feature overview.
One feature; data-feature is library, household or retro.
Local ownership, offline use, privacy and customisation.
A platform's status, formats and direct installer links.
Platform name, icon and optional status badge.
Download instructions and the release archive link.
Native details disclosures with common questions.
Project documentation, source and licence links.

name: button
description: A push button.

name: checkbox
description: A checkbox with its label.
parts: The tick or dash inside the box.

name: segmented
description: One choice from a few options shown side by side.

name: select
description: A dropdown choice; its list opens in a `select-popover`.
parts: The button that opens the list; carries `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`.

name: select-popover
description: The open list of a `select`, rendered in a portal.
parts: The tick on the selected option.

name: menu
description: A menu of actions, rendered in a portal: a button's dropdown, or a right click's menu at the pointer.
parts: An action; carries `data-focused` and `data-disabled`, and `data-tone="danger"` when it removes something.
A second line under an item's text.

name: slider
description: A value on a track.
parts: The filled part of the rail.

name: switch
description: An on/off toggle.

name: text-field
description: A single-line text input.
parts: The box around the icon and input.
The control beside the input, e.g. a Browse… button.

name: settings-section
description: A titled group of settings.
parts: Badges or actions at the end of the heading row.

name: setting-row
description: One setting: its label on the left, its controls on the right.

name: status-dot
description: A small coloured dot and label, e.g. Detected / Not found.

name: pill
description: A bordered chip with an icon, e.g. Off by default.

name: game-art
description: A game's cover, or a blank placeholder when it has none.

name: status-badge
description: A game's install status.

name: game-card
rendered: GameCard; the library's LibraryCard and the Web tab's tiles (app)
description: A game tile in a grid.
parts: The genre; on LibraryCard, the platform unless it is a PC one.
The row of facts under the title.
Shown instead of stores when you own it.
Shown when the managed copy is unavailable.
Badges and overlays contributed by plugins.
In selection mode, the check that shows whether the game is chosen.
In console mode, the paired device the game is running on.
On Home's Recently Played, the other device the game was last played on, in place of the subtitle.
Starting…, over the art from a double click or Play until the game runs, the launch fails or a question stops it.

name: hero
rendered: Hero; the home and game pages' hero sections (app)
description: The large featured-game banner.
parts: The coloured glow behind the content.
The gradient that keeps text readable.
The small label above the title.
The pulsing dot in the eyebrow.
A link to the game's own page on the web (a web game's).
On Home, the other device the game was last played on (in the meta).

name: shelf
description: A titled row of cards.

name: avatar
description: An account's picture: one of the shipped avatars, or the name's initials when its id is unknown or the image can't load.

name: error-notice
description: A failure, shown the same way everywhere: what failed and why, what to do, and the technical details behind a toggle.
parts: What couldn't be done, when given.
What failed and, when known, why.
What the user can do, one item each.
Recovery controls (e.g. Try again) and the details toggle.
The redacted technical details and the log reference.
The reference to find the failure in the log.

name: avatar-picker
description: A grid of the shipped avatars to choose one from (a radio group).
parts: An avatar to choose (an `avatar` inside); carries `data-selected`, `data-hovered` and `data-focus-visible`.
The tick on the chosen avatar.

name: app-shell
description: The window: sidebar, topbar, current view and persistent status bar.
parts: The column right of the sidebar.

name: status-bar
description: Persistent background activity, application version and an available Caskade update. IGDB and Hasheous are credited in Settings → About (`about`).
parts: The activity spinner; hidden while idle.
A concise description of current work or queue status.
A link to Settings → General once a check finds a new Caskade version; `data-status` is `available`, or `ready` once it is installed and waits for a restart.
With paired devices (#231): how many are in reach and the best way one is reached (a `peer-link`), linked to Settings → Devices; `data-status` is `lan`, `direct`, `relay`, `offline` or `syncing`.

name: backdrop
description: The decorative layer behind everything.

name: onboarding
description: First-run setup, shown in place of the app shell: a welcome, the questions (`language`, `folder`, `sources`, `mode`, and `account`, the admin's name, avatar and PIN), then the work they start (`setup`). Things arriving use `animate-rise`; the running task's sweep pauses with `--cs-motion-ambient`.
parts: The row at the top that moves the window.
Turns setup's sounds on and off.
The logo on the welcome screen, with its glow.
The games folder, its free space and its Change button.
Something to look for; `data-status` is `on` or `off`.
Desktop or console mode; React Aria's `data-selected` marks the choice.
A language, or System; React Aria's `data-selected` marks the choice.
Continue, Set up, or Open my library.
The step dots; each has `data-status` `active`, `done` or `next`.
The work being done; `data-status` is `running` or `done`.
Covers of the games found so far, behind the list.
How many games the library has.
One task; `data-task` names it, `data-status` is `waiting`, `running`, `done`, `warning` or `failed`.

name: sidebar
description: The navigation column.
parts: A link; the current one has `data-status="active"`.
The links under a link: the Library's filters, open (`data-open`) while the Library is.
A filter; the current one has `data-status="active"`.
How many games a filter has.

name: topbar
description: The bar above the view: search, quick actions and the window controls. It is the window's title bar: dragging it moves the window.
parts: The items at the end of the bar.
The number of running jobs; `data-status` is `active` or `needs-user`.
The number of unread notifications, apart from the jobs.
The signed-in account's button, which opens the account menu (an `avatar` inside).
Enters console mode, where Caskade draws no window controls (macOS, the browser preview).

name: window-controls
description: Minimize, maximize and close at the end of the topbar (Windows and Linux; macOS keeps its traffic lights). Each button carries `data-hovered` and `data-pressed`.
parts: Enters console mode (fullscreen, for a controller).
Maximizes the window, or restores it when maximized.

name: view-error
description: Shown in place of a view that failed to render, with the shell around it; or in place of the whole window when the shell itself failed, with the window controls.
parts: Try again and Open the library, or Reload.

name: console-shell
description: Console mode's window (`[data-mode="console"]` on the root): the console sidebar, top bar and view, and the button-hint bar. `data-cursor` is `hidden` while the pointer rests.
parts: The column right of the sidebar.

name: console-sidebar
description: Console mode's navigation: big targets.
parts: A link; the current one has `data-status="active"`.
The links under a link: the Library's filters, open (`data-open`) while the Library is.
A filter; the current one has `data-status="active"`.
How many games a filter has.
Plugin views that show in console mode.

name: console-topbar
description: Console mode's top bar: search and activity.
parts: The items at the end of the bar.
The number of running jobs; `data-status` is `active` or `needs-user`.
The number of unread notifications, apart from the jobs.
The signed-in account's button, which opens the account menu (an `avatar` inside).

name: notifications
description: Activity's notification feed (#198): game additions in hourly batches, failed jobs, updates on offer and plugins turned off, newest change first.
parts: The filters and Mark all read.
All or Unread; the current one has `data-selected`.
Marks read every item shown so far.
Shown when the feed (or its unread filter) is empty.
Newer and Older, when the feed has more than a page.

name: notification
description: One item of the notification feed. `data-category` is what it is about; `data-resolved` is set once its problem has cleared.
parts: When: a batch's first to last addition, else its last change.
Details: a batch's sources, a failure's error.
Open (the list, the game or the settings it is about) and Mark read or unread.
What it is about, once opened: a batch's games, the updates on offer.
One of them; `data-status` is `present`, `merged` (it links to the game it joined), `removed` or `other`.

name: hint-bar
description: What each controller button does where focus is. `data-glyphs` is the controller family in hand: `xbox`, `playstation`, `nintendo`, `generic`, or `keyboard`.
parts: One button and what it does; `data-action` is the action (`confirm`, `back`, `tab.next`, …).
The button's label; face buttons carry `data-tone` (`installed`, `danger`, `accent`, `warning`).

name: game-curtain
description: Console mode's black screen behind a running game: it fades in when a game starts, so the game's window takes over without Caskade minimizing, and fades out when the last game exits. Always present in console mode; `data-state` is `covered` while it is down.
parts: The guide button, which opens the quick menu over it.

name: shelf-row
description: A row of game cards that pages with LB/RB (Home's shelves).
parts: The LB/RB buttons, in console mode.
The link to every game in the shelf.

name: search
description: The game search; suggestions open in a `search-popover`.
parts: The box around the input; carries `data-focus-within`.
The shortcut that focuses it: Ctrl K, or in console mode the controller's search button.

name: search-popover
description: The search suggestions, rendered in a portal.
parts: The item that opens every result in the library.

name: view
description: The scrolling area that shows the current page.

name: settings-nav
description: Settings' sections: a vertical tab list beside the open section's panel, in desktop and console modes, grouped under headings, with the settings search above it. It stays in view while the panel scrolls, and scrolls on its own when the sections don't fit.
parts: A group's heading, before its sections (App, Library, …); not a stop for focus.
A section; the open one carries `data-selected`, and each `data-hovered`, `data-pressed` and `data-focus-visible`.
A section's name; long names wrap.

name: about
description: Settings → About: the IGDB and Hasheous credits first, side by side, then the app, its version and build, project links, and the links into `legal`.
parts: The list of data credits, directly under the heading.
One credit (IGDB, Hasheous): a link to the service, each with the same weight.
The app's name, logo and short description.
The version and build, from the app's build metadata.
Links to the project page, issue tracker and releases.
Links to each section of the Legal view.

name: legal
description: Settings → About → Legal: licences, open-source packages, terms and privacy policy, bundled for offline reading. One section shows at a time, at `/settings?tab=about&section=<id>`.
parts: A section; the open one carries `aria-current`.
A long text (a policy, a licence group's packages and texts): focusable, so keys and a pad scroll it.

name: system-stats
description: Settings → Statistics: this machine's CPU, GPUs, memory, network and storage capacity, live, as the same cards in desktop and console modes. `data-status` says whether readings are coming in.
parts: The line under it: live, waiting, not updating or unavailable, in words.
One metric (`data-metric`: `cpu`, `memory`, `gpu`, `network`, `storage`); focusable, so keys and a pad reach every card.
A utilization gauge (`role=meter`) with its percentage written inside.
A recent-history graph; a missed sample is a gap in its line.
Why a metric has no value: unsupported, no device or a failed sample.
A network interface and its rates; `data-kind` is `physical`, `virtual` or `loopback`.
A storage volume: its name, mount points and capacity.

name: panel
description: A framed panel inside a view.

name: collection-card
description: A collection tile.

name: platform-card
description: A platform in the library's breakdown of emulated games; opens its games.
parts: The hardware render on its glow.
Its maker and kind of machine.
When one of its games was last played.

name: game-row
description: A game in the library's compact table (the list layout).
parts: The game's icon, or its initial on generated art.
The game's title; links to the game and covers the row.
Shown when the managed copy is unavailable.
In selection mode, the check that shows whether the game is chosen.
Starting…, after the title from a double click or Play until the game runs, the launch fails or a question stops it.

name: alphabet-bar
description: The letters beside a long library sorted by title; each jumps to its games, and a drag jumps letter by letter.
parts: One initial (`#` for numbers and symbols); `data-selected` on the letter on screen, `data-disabled` when no game starts with it.

name: quick-look
description: A game at a glance over the current view: in desktop mode a column on the right that a click on a game opens, in console mode a modal from a pad's X on a card; X again plays it.
parts: Play, and View more beneath it.
Play, or Stop while it runs (a `button`).
View more: opens the game's page (a `button`).
Playtime, last play, size and release.

name: game-editor
description: A game's editor, from its menu's Edit… or its page's Edit details: its details as one draft saved together, its artwork, and tabs for its launch actions and scripts. A dialog in desktop mode, the whole window in console mode.
parts: The editor's sections: Details, Actions, Scripts.
One section; `data-selected` on the open one, `data-dirty` while it holds unsaved changes.
One field, with `data-field` naming it (`title`, `description`, `tags`, …), `data-manual` when its value is the user's and refreshes keep it, and `data-invalid` when the last save was refused for it.
Marks a value the user set.
Puts a field or an artwork kind back to its automatic value (a `button`).
Why a field wasn't saved, with the conflict choices.
Keeps the user's value over the one saved meanwhile (a `button`).
A list field's values and its add field.
Removes a value from its list (a `button`).
Who decides an artwork kind's image: automatic, chosen by the user, or none.
One kind of artwork (`data-kind`: `cover`, `hero`, `icon`; `data-choice`: `automatic`, `chosen`, `removed`; `data-drop-active` while an image is dragged over it).
The image that kind shows now.
An image a source supplied, to choose (a `button`; `data-selected` on the one shown).
Shows no image of that kind (a `button`).
Closes the editor, asking first when there are unsaved changes (a `button`).

name: manual-game
description: Adds a game by hand from Add game: one on this computer or behind a URI, started where it is, or a title-only record; games that may be the same offer to join or keep apart.
parts: What it starts: the path or URI field, Browse and the drop area (`data-drop-active` while a file is dragged over).
The program, arguments, folder or URI it will start.
Games that may be the same one.
Adds the target to that game instead (a `button`).
Why the target can't be added, or adding failed.
Adds the game, or keeps it separate from the duplicates (a `button`).

name: selection-bar
description: The bar of a library or collection view in selection mode: how many games are chosen, choosing the loaded ones or all of them, clearing, the bulk editor and Done.
parts: Chooses the games loaded so far (a `button`).
Chooses every game the view finds, with how many (a `button`).

name: games-refresh-start
description: Starts refreshing the chosen games' details and artwork from the built-in sources: missing details only, or the automatic ones fetched again.

name: games-refresh
description: The refresh of chosen games' details in Activity: progress, counts, Cancel, and retrying failed games or continuing a cancelled refresh.
parts: Missing details only, or automatic details refreshed.
Updated, unchanged, not found on IGDB, skipped and failed games.
Refreshes the games that failed again (a `button`).
Refreshes the games a cancelled refresh left (a `button`).

name: bulk-editor
description: One edit on the chosen games: the fields to change, a preview of what changes in which game, and what saved.
parts: The fields, each changed only when ticked.
A list field's values and its add field.
Removes a value from its list (a `button`).
How many games change, already have it, can't take it or are gone.
One game and what changes in it.
A game that can't take the edit, and why.
Status, Back or Cancel, and Preview, Apply or Done.
Back to the fields, or Cancel (a `button`).

name: game-editor-discard
description: Asks before an editor with unsaved changes closes: Keep editing or Discard.

name: game-actions
description: The game editor's Actions tab (#178): a release's launch actions, its own launch first, with the form for the one chosen and what Play starts.
parts: What Play starts: one of the play actions, or Ask each time.
One action; `data-kind` is `play` or `utility`, `data-selected` on the one in the form.
Says the release's own launch comes from its source and how to change it.
What an emulator, web or plugin action starts, which the form doesn't change.
A path with Browse…; `data-drop-active` while a dropped file is over it.
A list of values, one field each: arguments, program names.
The environment variables, a name and a value per row.
Which Proton build a Windows program runs with: Automatic (the best installed) or one build.
Which programs are the game, for a play action.
Why the last save, order, delete or default change was refused.
Deletes the action; pressed once more to confirm (a `button`).

name: game-saves
description: The game editor's Saves tab (#238): one release's save locations on this device, automatic or the user's own, and the manifest game it matches. Files and folders dropped on it are added.
parts: What the locations come from; `data-match` is `unknown`, `matched` or `ambiguous`.
Says whether the automatic locations or the user's own are in use.
One location; `data-kind` is `file`, `folder` or `registry`, with its file count.
A location's path or registry key.
Shown when the release has no save locations.
What couldn't be resolved on this device.
Why the locations couldn't load or the last save was refused.

name: scripts
description: One scope's lifecycle scripts (#180), in Settings → Scripts, an emulator profile and the game editor: the scripts, the chosen one's form, its test and the order a launch runs every scope's scripts in.
parts: One script; `data-enabled` is `false` for one that's off, `data-selected` on the one in the form.
A path with Browse… (the program, the working folder); `data-drop-active` while a dropped file is over it.
A program's arguments, one field each.
Why the last save, order or delete was refused.
Deletes the script; pressed once more to confirm (a `button`).
Test and Cancel test, and the last test's result.
A test's outcome; `data-status` is how it ended (`succeeded`, `failed`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `not_started`).
A test's standard output or errors.
The order a launch runs scripts in, every scope's.
One step; `data-inherited` when it comes from another scope, `data-enabled` `false` when it's off.

name: play-choice
description: On a game's page, under Play: which of the release's play actions Play starts, and its tools (#178).
parts: The release's tools, one button each.

name: tool-failed
description: Says why a game's tool didn't start.

name: screenshot-viewer
description: A game's screenshots one at a time, filling the window, opened from its page; arrows, a swipe, a pad's left/right or LB/RB step through them.
parts: The area the screenshot fills; a swipe on it steps.
Every screenshot, small, to jump to one.
One screenshot in the strip; `data-selected` on the one shown.

name: videos
description: A game's videos (IGDB's trailers) in a row on its page and its Store page; each plays in the video window.
parts: One video's button: its thumbnail and name.
The play mark over the thumbnail.

name: osk
description: The on-screen keyboard a pad types with; it types into the focused field, which keeps focus.
parts: The field's text as it is typed.
A key; `data-key` is its character or what it does (`shift`, `layer`, `backspace`, `space`, `left`, `right`, `done`), `data-focused` is the pad's place, `data-selected` an active shift.

name: type-search
description: Search from a keyboard, RetroArch style: a centred overlay with the text being typed and how many games match, opened by typing anywhere outside a text field or by `/`.
parts: The keys for the results, cancelling and deleting.

name: folder-browser
description: Console mode's file and folder picker, in place of the native dialogs a controller can't drive. A opens a folder or picks a file, B cancels, LB/RB go to the previous and next place, LT/RT page through the folder, Start picks the folder shown. `data-kind` is what it picks.
parts: The folder shown, as a path.
Home, the filesystem root and mounted drives.
One place; the one the folder is in has `data-status="active"`.
Why a folder couldn't be opened.
A folder or file; `data-kind` is `folder` or `file`. Files that can't be picked carry `data-disabled`.
Shown in a folder with nothing in it.
Cancel, and in folder mode Select this folder.

name: store-links
description: Links to the stores that sell a game.

name: peer-link
description: How another device is reached (#225, #231): an icon and a word. `data-status` is `lan` (on this network), `direct` (over the internet), `relay` (through a relay) or `offline`.

name: paired-device
description: A device paired with this one: its icon, name, how it is reached, its last sync, Sync now and (for an admin) Forget. `data-status` is how it is reached.
parts: Its OS and the last sync, or that it is syncing now.
Shown when the last sync didn't reach it.

name: transfer
description: A game copied between two of the user's devices (#233): its title, the other device, how it is reached and its progress. `data-status` is `running`, `waitingDirect` (game files wait for a direct path), `done` or `failed`.

name: share
rendered: SharesList in Settings → Devices → Copies and shares (app)
description: A game this device shared once with someone else (#246, #247): its title and size, Copy link and Stop sharing while it runs (Forget after), what it is doing and who received it. `data-status` is `preparing` (its files are being read; the link works already), `ready`, `failed`, `stopped` or `expired`.
parts: What the share is doing: reading its files, until when the link works, or that it stopped.
Who opened the link, each with how far they got.

name: share-recipient
description: Someone who opened a share's link (#247): their device's name, whether they help others receive it, and a bar of how far they got. `data-status` is `receiving`, `away` (not connected now) or `done`.

name: received-share
rendered: SharesList in Settings → Devices → Copies and shares (app)
description: A game someone shared with this device (#249): its title and sharer, and the Help others receive it switch. `data-status` is `receiving`, `serving` (it helps the share's other recipients) or `done`.

name: share-game
description: Share with someone… (#247): how long the link works, then the link with Copy (and, in console mode, a QR code), what the share is doing, who received it, and Stop sharing.
parts: The link as a QR code, in console mode.

name: receive-share
description: Add game → Receive a shared game… (#247): the link, what its sharer says it shares, Help others receive it, and Receive.

name: share-info
description: What a share link shares, as its sharer says (#247, #248): who, what, its size and build, until when the link works; for a save, web game or ROM, where it goes here; for a collection, which of its games this device has. `data-status` is `direct`, or `relayOnly` when only a relay reaches the sharer and files wait for a direct connection.
parts: Where a save, web game or ROM goes on this device.
A shared collection's games, each with whether it's here (`data-status`).

name: pair-device
description: Pairing over any view (#226, #231): the code both devices show, for a pairing this device or the other one started; or a `caskade://pair` link opened from outside, waiting for an admin.
parts: The six-digit code, split in two; larger in console mode.
An opened pairing link; `data-status` is `valid` or `expired`.

name: account-picker
description: Who is playing: the accounts to sign in as, at start and after Switch account, and the PIN pad for a locked one. `data-step` is `accounts` or `pin`.
parts: The bar along the top: it drags the window, and holds the window controls.
An account's tile; `data-status="locked"` when a PIN locks it. The last account to sign in has `data-focus-default`.
The lock on a PIN-locked account's tile.
Back from the PIN pad to the accounts.

name: pin-pad
description: PIN entry: a field for keys and a number pad for a controller (A types a digit, B deletes, Start confirms). A wrong PIN shakes the field and clears it; after too many, `locked` counts the wait down.
parts: Why the PIN was refused, or how long to wait.

name: account-menu
description: The head of the menu the topbar's avatar opens: who is signed in. Its actions are the `menu`'s items.

name: account-list
description: Settings → Accounts, for admins: every account, with Edit and Delete.
parts: Its name; the signed-in account's says so.
Its role, whether a PIN locks it, and what it may do.
Asks before deleting the account and its collections (a `button`).

name: account-editor
description: The dialog that adds or changes an account: its name, avatar, role and PIN, and for a standard account what it may change and its age limit.
parts: The avatar choice (an `avatar-picker`) and its label.
A standard account's permissions: Install games, one switch per Settings section, the maximum age rating and unrated games.

name: account-profile
description: Settings → My profile: the signed-in account's own name, avatar and PIN.
parts: The avatar choice (an `avatar-picker`) and its label.
The PIN's row: set, change or remove it, after the current PIN.

name: addon-catalogue
description: Settings → Plugins' catalogue of curated plugins and themes: what each means here, searchable and by kind, from the last fetch when offline.
parts: Check for updates: fetches the catalogue again (a `button`).
When the catalogue was fetched, offline or why the last check failed.
Whether to check for updates when Settings opens (a `switch`).
What the add-on means here (`data-state`: `available`, `installed`, `updateAvailable` or `incompatible`).

name: addon-details
description: A catalogue add-on's details: screenshots, description as text, compatibility, the release an install gets, and installing, updating, applying and removing it.
parts: One screenshot, a thumbnail the app re-encoded.
In place of a screenshot that couldn't load.
The description, always shown as text.
Why the add-on doesn't fit here, or what it lacks.
The release an install gets: version, date, OSes, modes and permissions.
What the add-on means here (`data-state`: `available`, `installed`, `updateAvailable` or `incompatible`).
What the last install did (`data-outcome`: `installed` or `failed`), or a release refused before.
Asks before removing; for a plugin, whether to keep its settings and data.
Skips this update, or offers it again (a `button`).
Makes an installed theme the one in use (a `button`).

name: achievements
description: A game page's achievements: one store account's set at a time, its counts and how its last fetch went, and every achievement with its state, progress, unlock time, rarity and points where the service gives them. Hidden achievements stay concealed until unlocked or revealed.
parts: Refresh achievements: fetches the game's sets now (a `button`).
Which store account's set is shown, when there are several (a `segmented`).
The set's service and account, and when it was last fetched.
